    AI Overview
    To build a creative portfolio submission form, gather contact information, project links (URL or PDF), and case study details. A well-structured form filters high-quality submissions and minimizes back-and-forth communication. 
    Here is an effective template structure to include in your form: 
    1. Applicant Information
    • Full Name
    • Email Address
    • Phone Number
    • Primary Creative Discipline (e.g., Graphic Design, Copywriting, Illustration)
    • Link to Personal Website or Portfolio Homepage 
    2. Project Details
    • Project Title: What is the name of the project?
    • Description: Briefly describe the problem you solved, your role, and the project's goal (maximum 250 words).
    • Contribution: Were you the sole creator, or did you work in a team?
    • Tools Used: List the primary media, tools, or software used.
    • Upload/Link: Space to attach a PDF or paste a link to a password-protected page, Google Drive, or Figma file. 
    3. Professional Questions (Optional)
    • What is your availability or preferred project scope?
    • How did you hear about this opportunity?
    • Please provide a brief Artist Statement (maximum 200 words). 
    4. Recommended Tools to Build Your Form
    You can easily create and embed submission forms using these tools: 
    • Typeform: Best for a conversational, user-friendly experience that handles file uploads.
    • Google Forms: A simple, free solution that integrates directly with Google Drive for easy file collection.
    • Jotform: Offers hundreds of customizable templates specifically for design submissions and portfolios. 
    If you want, let me know:
    • What specific role or opportunity (e.g., college admission, job application, freelance client) this form is for?
    • What types of media (e.g., video files, large 3D images, writing) you need applicants to submit?
    I can tailor the questions to fit your exact needs and file size limits.

    People also ask
    How do I submit my art portfolio?
    Look for an area on their website where they mention how they want portfolios submitted. Some galleries want an email, others a mailed in portfolio. You should abide by the method that they ask for or else you risk getting off on the wrong foot.
